propositions: T11's unconditional post-rollback-state finding paragraph generates near-identical tautological advisories that are inapplicable to append-only stores, drowning rare critical findings like data-loss bugs.
The post-rollback applicability rule must be portable across all persistence stacks (SQL, event stores, document databases, config formats) without naming specific store technology.

Post-rollback findings should only be raised when a plan changes interpretation of existing records, rewrites records in place, removes/narrows read paths, or performs one-way transformations with no back-out.

Purely additive backward-compatible changes (new record types, optional fields, new tables/columns with defaults) that existing readers ignore do not qualify for post-rollback findings since residual data is the norm in append-only systems.
